name: Shivamogga
headline: Hostel conditions for SC/ST students and child marriage drive exits; police now track dropouts.
summary: The state child-rights commission noted high dropout among SC/ST students in social-welfare hostels in Shivamogga, citing poor living conditions and food. Child marriage is a persistent threat, with 79 cases recorded in 2023-24, and police and the education department are working to trace dropped-out youth. The report's claim about schools forcing weak students to register as private candidates is about a Chikkamagaluru school and has been moved there.

reasons.detail: The child-rights commission noted high dropout among marginalised students in welfare hostels, citing unlivable conditions and poor food.
79 child marriages were recorded in 2023-24, and officials avert several each year.
Police tracking in 2026 found children leaving school because families needed income; the drive focused on home visits, counselling and readmission into government schools.
Alongside poverty, children who struggled academically lost confidence and stopped attending, according to the police campaign's account of why the 946 identified children had left.
After 23 child pregnancies surfaced, the Collector ordered closer watch on dropouts, girls often absent from school or college, and families at risk of child marriage.

reasons.factor: Paid weekend work pulling students out
reasons.detail: Teachers in malnad degree colleges found students from Shivamogga and neighbouring districts skipping classes for paid catering work in Bengaluru, a trend said to have grown after Covid. College-level evidence.

reasons.factor: Tribal-area school without teachers or toilets
reasons.detail: A tribal-majority government school at Elige in Sagar taluk reportedly had no permanent teachers for eight years and lacked proper toilets for girls; this was a primary school.

responses.text: Police and the education department are jointly tracing dropouts to bring them back to school.

District police 'Back to School' campaign collected dropout details, verified status, made home visits, counselled families and secured government-school admissions; tracking of re-enrolled children continues.
District Collector directed intensified monitoring of dropouts, frequently absent girls and at-risk families, and FIRs against those facilitating child marriages.
